methodology.timing: Monotonic elapsed wall time; construction excluded except load; runtime GC during measured operations included. Warmup occurs before timing and allocation baselines.
methodology.process_model: Each language/sample is a fresh process; seven alternating-language-order repetitions per workload. Workload scenario order is fixed.
methodology.allocation: OCaml Gc.allocated_bytes and Go MemStats.TotalAlloc deltas; runtime-specific allocated bytes, not comparable retained heap or peak RSS.
methodology.variation: Population CV is pstdev/mean for the observed seven samples; sample CV uses n-1 denominator. IQR uses inclusive quartiles. Neither is a confidence interval.
methodology.ratio: Go median microseconds per logical operation divided by OCaml median; descriptive for the specified workload only.
methodology.resource_scope: GNU time stage RSS covers the controller/builds/children maximum and is not a per-language memory comparison.
methodology.input_regeneration: Current local harness fingerprint equals measured source; model/policy text and canonical schema/request JSON regenerated and SHA-checked independently from receipts. Checksums separately derived from workload outcomes and operation counts.
methodology.protocol_validation_scope: Verified measured driver source rejects nonzero exit, any benchmark stderr, malformed five-field TSV/newline, wrong scenario/count/checksum and nonfinite durations/allocations. Raw individual TSV lines were captured by the driver and not retained; audit validates stored sample arrays, aggregate stdout and zero stage exits.

focused_vs_primary.interpretation: Longer samples support timing precision but also change runtime/GC amortization. Go per-operation medians are lower in the longer batch; no GC-count instrumentation isolates the cause. Both receipts remain separate; neither selects a universal speed ratio.

role_request_reuse_control.interpretation: Same model, policy, schema, one permission row and full identity graph. Cold uses unique subjects after one disjoint sentinel warmup; warm reuses u0 after repeated warmup. Cold also formats each subject and constructs each request inside timing, while warm preconstructs its request. This changes request reuse and formatting as well as Go g-cache hits; it is not a pure isolated g-cache ablation.

limits: Shared host with CPU 2 affinity, not exclusive CPU reservation; ondemand governor and host load recorded. No maximum-throughput, hardware-general or language-general claim.
Only declared supported Casbin subset and named workload fixtures; parity checksums do not prove arbitrary models or request sequences.
Fixed scenario order and filesystem warming can affect results; language order alternates but scenario order is not randomized.
Go g tuple memoization, OCaml graph traversal, typed object representation and mutation contracts differ; these are implementation/API workload comparisons.
Scan budget caps policy rows times logical operations, not internal effector work. Go last-match priority at 10000 rows performs 99990001 merge-slot checks per enforcement, based on pinned source.
Below-1ms samples are flagged, including 10000-row Go management (~1us/op; population CV about 9.5%). Do not report the computed mutation ratio as a precise or general update advantage.
Cold role workloads at 10 and 100 identities have short samples and unstable variation; 10000-identity cold/control are the useful request-reuse comparison.
Focused first-match longer batches lower Go per-operation costs relative to the 500-operation matrix. Batch/GC dynamics may contribute; no isolated cause is established.
Warm-role control also changes subject formatting, request allocation and working-set reuse; not a pure g-cache ablation.
Allocation counters have different runtime accounting; resources are whole-stage measurements. No comparable peak heap claim.
Seven serial repetitions on one host are descriptive evidence; no significance test or population confidence guarantee.

priority_source_evidence.interpretation: Pinned Go allocates policy-length effect/match arrays and invokes a reverse full-buffer merge at each evaluated row; OCaml streams ordered row outcomes. This explains workload complexity differences without requiring an authorization semantic difference.
